lessons.title: Asking and Telling Age
lessons.body:
Asking age in Mandarin is straightforward: 'nÇ duÅ dÃ  le?' (How old are you?). This is informal and used for peers or younger people. For formal situations, say 'nÃ­n duÅ dÃ  niÃ¡njÃ¬?' Note: 'le' indicates a change of state, often used with age.

In Africa, age is sometimes a sensitive topic, but in Chinese culture, it's common to ask. However, be respectful. If someone asks your age, answer clearly. Practice numbers 1â100 with 'suÃ¬'. For example, 'wÇ sÄnshÃ­ suÃ¬' (I am 30). 'TÄ sÃ¬shÃ­'Ã¨r suÃ¬' (He is 42). To ask about someone else: 'tÄ duÅ dÃ  le?' (How old is he/she?). For a child: 'nÇ Ã©rzi jÇ suÃ¬ le?' Learn to talk about age in context. For business, age may indicate experience. Say 'wÇ yÇjÄ«ng gÅngzuÃ² shÃ­ niÃ¡n le' (I have worked for 10 years). Or 'wÇ cÃ³ng shÃ¬ zhÃ¨ge hÃ¡ngyÃ¨ Ã¨rshÃ­ niÃ¡n le' (I have been in this industry for 20 years). When meeting new people, you might exchange ages. Practice with a friend: ask and answer. For official documents, you might need to write your birth date and age. Practice writing: 'wÇ yÄ« jiÇ bÄ wÇ niÃ¡n chÅ«shÄng, jÄ«nniÃ¡n sÄnshÃ­jiÇ suÃ¬' (I was born in 1985, this year I am 39). Use a calculator to check. In conversations, listen for 'suÃ¬' to catch age. Also learn 'niÃ¡njÃ¬' (age, years) in formal contexts. For example, 'nÃ­n de niÃ¡njÃ¬ shÃ¬?' (Your age?). Respond politely: 'wÇ wÇshÃ­ suÃ¬' (I am 50). Practice with audio resources. Knowing how to discuss age helps build relationships and shows respect.
